question.text: `Bharat Cements Ltd` reports the following for FY 2024-25: net worth INR 480 crore, turnover INR 1,200 crore, net profit INR 4.5 crore. Under Section 135 of the Companies Act 2013, is CSR applicability triggered?

answer.text: No — all three thresholds must be breached simultaneously
No — net profit is below INR 5 crore, which is the controlling threshold
Yes — any ONE of the three thresholds (net worth ≥ INR 500 cr, turnover ≥ INR 1,000 cr, net profit ≥ INR 5 cr) triggers applicability, and turnover crosses INR 1,000 cr
Yes — but only voluntarily, since net worth and net profit are below the statutory levels

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 135(1) of the Companies Act 2013 triggers CSR applicability if, in the immediately preceding financial year, a company meets ANY ONE of the following thresholds: net worth of at least INR 500 crore, turnover of at least INR 1,000 crore, or net profit of at least INR 5 crore. Bharat Cements crosses the turnover limb (INR 1,200 crore ≥ INR 1,000 crore), so CSR is mandatory and 2% of three-year average net profit must be spent. The Trap: Option A reverses the OR into an AND (a common trap). Option B focuses only on the net-profit limb, but any one threshold alone is sufficient. Option D treats CSR as voluntary, but once any threshold is crossed it is a statutory obligation. Note: The cited SIA workbook mentions CSR spending as 2% of company net profit and the CSR impact-assessment rule, but does not on the pages checked provide the Section 135 applicability thresholds (net worth INR 500 crore, turnover INR 1,000 crore, net profit INR 5 crore). The threshold framing above is drawn from the Companies Act 2013 itself rather than a workbook-page citation.
